entries.reason: the name is in the port's image and nothing applies it: the protocol this file declares carries the selector, and no call site in the tree sends it, so the row is not a claim that the release has nothing. The release is not the reason either, and saying so was wrong in the row before this one: 6.1.3 does carry SystemConfiguration's reachability, whose create and callback first appear at 3.0, and this same library already reads it for a task that waits for connectivity. What those flags answer is whether the host is reachable and over which kind of interface, while the header's message says the system has determined that a better route to the host exists; a change in those flags sent under that name would be the port's own inference reported as the system's determination, and the header's own warning that a new task may still fail is what such a report invites a caller to get wrong
entries.effect: never sent: a delegate that implements -URLSession:betterRouteDiscoveredForStreamTask: is simply not called, for the whole life of the task. The protocol around it is there, so NSProtocolFromString answers the name and a class may declare conformance, which is what makes this a message that loads and nothing sends
